'''Cecilia Wen-ya Lo''' ({{zh|t=羅聞亞}}<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://aims.cuhk.edu.hk/converis/portal/detail/Person/64889643?lang=zh_HK|title=羅聞亞教授|website=Chinese University of Hong Kong|language=zh|access-date=2020-08-17}}</ref>) is a professor and the [[F. Sargent Cheever]] Chair of Developmental Biology at the [[University of Pittsburgh]]. Her research focuses on the study of [[congenital heart defect]]s.<ref name=pitt>{{Cite web|last=Srikameswaran|first=Anita|url=https://www.chronicle.pitt.edu/story/cecilia-lo-appointed-chair-new-developmental-biology-department-pitt-medical-school|title=Cecilia Lo Appointed Chair of New Developmental Biology Department in Pitt Medical School {{!}} Pitt Chronicle {{!}} University of Pittsburgh|website=www.chronicle.pitt.edu|language=en|access-date=2017-05-19}}</ref><ref name=devbio>{{Cite web|url=http://devbio.pitt.edu/subsites/lo/index.html|title=Cecilia Lo, Ph.D.|website=Department of Developmental Biology, University of Pittsburgh|access-date=18 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170430020643/http://www.devbio.pitt.edu/subsites/lo/index.html|archive-date=30 April 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Education==
Lo received her bachelor's degree in biology in 1974 from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], where she worked with [[David Baltimore]]. She received her Ph.D. in 1979 from [[Rockefeller University]].<ref name=pitt />

==Academic career==
After a period on the faculty at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], Lo joined the [[National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute]] (NHLBI), one of the [[United States National Institutes of Health]], to serve as chief of the Laboratory of Developmental Biology in 2001. Three years later, she became the director of the NHLBI's Genetics and Developmental Biology Center. In 2009, she and her husband, fellow NIH researcher [[Rocky Tuan]], were recruited to the [[University of Pittsburgh]]. Lo became the founding chair of the newly established Department of Developmental Biology and is the [[F. Sargent Cheever]] professor.<ref name=pitt /><ref name=devbio /><ref name=trib>{{Cite web|url=http://triblive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/news/health/s_621701.html|title=Husband-wife team leaves NIH to start new medical centers at Pitt|last=Heinrichs|first=Allison M.|website=TribLIVE.com|language=en-US|access-date=2017-05-19}}</ref>

==Research==
Lo's research focuses on the [[genetics]] and [[developmental biology]] of [[congenital heart defect]]s. Her research group relies on [[mouse model]]s for investigation of genetic causes of congenital heart disease and also engages in [[translational research]]. They have developed particular interest in the functional role of [[cilia]] in heart development and in contributions of genetic defects in ciliary function to clinical outcomes, especially with respect to cases of [[heterotaxy]].<ref name=devbio /><ref name=upmc2009>{{Cite web|url=http://www.upmc.com/media/NewsReleases/2009/Pages/bench-to-bassinet.aspx|title=Pitt Team Part of $100 Million NHLBI 'Bench to Bassinet' Effort in Congenital Heart Disease|website=www.upmc.com|language=en|access-date=2017-05-19}}</ref><ref name=upmc2015>{{Cite web|url=http://www.upmc.com/media/NewsReleases/2015/Pages/cilia-congenital-heart-disease.aspx|title=Pitt Team Identifies Genes that Play Critical Role in the Development of Congenital Heart Disease|website=www.upmc.com|language=en|access-date=2017-05-19}}</ref>

Lo and Tuan co-edited a three-volume book titled ''Developmental Biology Protocols''.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Developmental Biology Protocols : Volume I|last=Tuan|first=Rocky S.|last2=Lo|first2=Cecilia W.|date=2000|publisher=Humana Press|isbn=9780896038523|oclc=756436545|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/developmentalbio00rock_1}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Developmental biology protocols. Volume II|last=S.|first=Tuan, Rocky|last2=W.|first2=Lo, Cecilia|date=2000|publisher=Humana Press|isbn=9780896038530|oclc=170934659|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/developmentalbio00rock}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Developmental biology protocols.
